subject: SLA baseline & exception credit mechanics — review of proposed template
messages:
From: Alex Turner <alex.turner@nimbuspay.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 3 Sep 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: SLA baseline & exception credit mechanics — review of proposed template

Jonas / team —

Thanks for sending the draft SLA template over this morning. We ran it by engineering and procurement and have two areas where we need clarity / an ask:

1) Uptime baseline: 99.95% at the monthly level is fine generally, but for scheduled maintenance that hits more than one EU region we need an explicit carve-out and an alternative availability floor rather than counting it against the same monthly window. Can you point us to how that would be handled?

2) Credits: The remedy table looks like a single linear credit scale. Our finance team prefers a floor on monthly credits for business-critical profiles (we call them "Tier A routes") and a separate cap for non-critical traffic. Practically: if a Tier A route hits the 99.7% band we'd like an assurance the monthly credit does not drop below 8% of that route's monthly invoice.

We attached a short table that shows how Nimbus classifies routes and a sample P&L effect. Can we schedule 30 minutes to go through the logic and see if there is a middle ground?

Appreciate it —
Alex
Director, Cloud Ops
NimbusPay
[Attachment: Nimbus_Route_Classifications.xlsx (xlsx)]

From: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>
To: Alex Turner <alex.turner@nimbuspay.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 3 Sep 2026 10:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: SLA baseline & exception credit mechanics — review of proposed template

Alex —

Thanks, and good questions. Quick replies first, then I put Laura on a note with the proposed language edits.

1) Maintenance carve-out: we can add a regional maintenance carve-out clause that treats cross-region scheduled maintenance as a separate categorized event. In practice that means: any scheduled maintenance affecting >1 region will be declared at least 72 hours in advance, excluded from the monthly uptime calculation for the affected regions, and a separate "maintenance window" metric will be returned to Nimbus for transparency. I'll attach suggested wording and the exception logic table.

2) Tiered credit floors/caps: Redwood's standard remedy matrix is designed to balance financial predictability and moral hazard. That said, we can offer a negotiated floor for Tier A routes, expressed as a percentage of the route's billed amount, with an offset that reduces the general pool cap to keep overall exposure bounded. Suggested approach:
- Tier A floor: 8% of monthly invoice for the route at the 99.7% band.
- Overall customer cap: maintain an aggregate monthly cap (e.g., 30% of total monthly invoice) to protect against a cascading event.

Laura, can you draft the specific SLA clause and a short exhibit that ties these numbers to the Remedy Matrix? Marissa, please add the revised cap math and a pro forma exposure calc.

Happy to hop on a call — I have a slot tomorrow 11:00–11:30 PT.

Best,
Jonas Weber
Senior Account Executive
Redwood Inference
[Attachment: SLA_Template_v3.pdf (pdf)]

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>, Alex Turner <alex.turner@nimbuspay.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 4 Sep 2026 08:40:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: SLA baseline & exception credit mechanics — review of proposed template

Alex / Jonas / Marissa —

Following up with the drafted exhibit and proposed clause language. See the attached Exception_Logic_Table.xlsx (sheet 1 is the carve-out rules, sheet 2 is the credit-floor mapping). Key points:

- Regional maintenance carve-out (section 2.3.1): we exclude scheduled maintenance that impacts >1 region from the monthly uptime calculation for each impacted region provided Redwood issues a notification at least 72 hours in advance; such events will be tracked in the monthly availability report and will instead be recorded in a separate maintenance log.

- Tier A route floor (section 4.2a): for any route classified by Nimbus as Tier A, Redwood will guarantee a minimum credit equal to 8% of that route's monthly charges when that route falls into the 99.7%–99.5% band. If multiple bands are crossed in the month, the highest applicable remedy applies.

- Aggregate cap (section 4.5): to limit exposure we propose an aggregate monthly cap equal to 30% of the customer's total monthly invoice across all routes (this cap is applied after per-route floors are computed). We included an example pro forma calculation in the spreadsheet.

Marissa, note the cap math is in the exposure tab. Alex — please review and confirm whether the 72-hour notice and the 8% floor are acceptable starting points. If Nimbus wants a lower aggregate cap, we can iterate on the per-route floor to preserve expected financial exposure.

Best,
Laura Bennett
Head of Contracts — Redwood Inference
[Attachment: Exception_Logic_Table.xlsx (xlsx)]

From: Alex Turner <alex.turner@nimbuspay.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Nate Reid <nate.reid@nimbuspay.com>
Date: Tue, 7 Sep 2026 16:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: SLA baseline & exception credit mechanics — review of proposed template

Laura / Jonas —

Thanks for the fast turnaround and for putting the exhibit together. The team reviewed internally and here are Nimbus' counterpoints:

- 72-hour notice is workable for planned maintenance; however we'd like a guarantee that emergency cross-region maintenance (rare but possible) will have a defined mitigation path and a separate, smaller credit (not treated as a full exclusion). Suggest adding an "emergency cross-region mitigation" row in the table with a 48–72 hour retrospective report and a fixed 2% monthly credit if invoked.

- The 8% floor for Tier A at the 99.7% band is in line with our expectation, but finance asks that the floor be applied per customer invoice (i.e., not per-route) up to an internal Tier A subcap of 15% to avoid disproportionate payouts when many Tier A routes are impacted simultaneously.

- Regarding the aggregate 30% cap: we can accept this if Redwood will provide a quarterly exposure report and agree to a joint review if more than two months in a rolling quarter approach >20% exposure.

If those three points look feasible, procurement will push this through our internal legal and we can aim to finalize the exhibit next week.

Would appreciate Laura or Marissa acknowledging the emergency credit row and the per-invoice floor cap so I can brief our GC.

Cheers,
Alex Turner
Director, Cloud Ops
NimbusPay
[Attachment: Nimbus_Impact_Summary.pdf (pdf)]
